wi_01_september_wall.blurb: A secluded wall below the East Bluff rim at Devil's Lake, near Baraboo, usually reached from the top of the bluff instead of from the lake side. It holds 23 routes, almost all traditional with a few top-rope lines. Grades begin around 5.4 and reach the low 5.11s, but most fall between 5.7 and 5.9, which suits climbers who are comfortable placing their own gear on moderate lines. The lines are short, the tallest being roughly 45 feet. Expect a quiet, out-of-the-way feel compared with the better-known faces around the lake.

wi_main_cliff_west.blurb: The west face of the main cliff at Rattlesnake Mound, a sandstone bluff line in central Wisconsin with boulders scattered around its base. The face has a lower and an upper tier and holds 23 problems and routes: a mix of low-grade trad and top-rope lines, plus eight boulder problems running from easy to V7, mostly V1 to V5. The roped lines stay on gentle to moderate ground, nothing harder than about 5.10. It faces the parking area, so the walk from the car is short, and it works well as part of a wider day wandering the bluffs.
wi_main_cliff_west.parking_note: Leave the car at the lot near the saddle, then walk a short way to the bluffs.

wi_04_great_chimney_area.blurb: Cliffs lining the West Bluff Trail on both sides of Prospect Point at Devil's Lake, in the Prospect Point Rampart, which holds some of the longest lines in the park. There are 23 routes, nearly all traditional with a few top-rope options. This is a steeper, harder collection than most of the lake: only a handful are below 5.9, while around half the routes sit in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a couple of mid-grade crack classics among them. The lines are sustained and climb above talus, so it appeals to experienced trad leaders rather than beginners.

wi_02_y_crack_wall.blurb: The most-visited wall at Necedah (Petenwell Rock), a large sandstone crag rising from an old lake bed in central Wisconsin. A Y-shaped crack splits the middle of a steep face that leans out at about 20 degrees, with bolted lines on either side. There are 23 routes, 16 of them trad and 7 sport, ranging from an easy tower route up to 5.13, though the weight sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. A nearby tower offers gentler options. Both gear leaders and bolt clippers can find a worthwhile line here.
wi_02_y_crack_wall.approach: A short walk back through the woods and uphill from the parking area leads to the wall, which stands next to a prominent tower.

wi_east_side_backbone_ridge.blurb: A bouldering area on the east flank of Backbone Ridge in Governor Dodge State Park, near Dodgeville. The climbing is on a hillside cliff band, mostly shaded and a little shorter than the west side of the ridge. There are 23 problems, from a beginner-friendly easy line up to a V9, with most between V0 and V4 and a few stiffer ones at V6 and above. Sandstone blocks and edges make it a good place to wander with a crash pad, particularly in warm weather when the shade helps.
wi_east_side_backbone_ridge.parking_note: Leave the car near the restrooms by the group camp area, then walk up the hill.
wi_east_side_backbone_ridge.approach: From the restrooms, go uphill, turn right and follow the cliff band along to the problems.

wi_5_4_doorway_rocks_minor_mass.blurb: A trad formation near the top of the Potholes Trail on Devil's Lake's East Bluff, just west of Red Rocks and separated from the Major Mass by a gully. It has two distinct levels and a South Tower of about 80 feet. Of 22 listings, most are traditional lines, with one top-rope route and one boulder problem. Grades start around 5.3, cluster between 5.4 and 5.10, and finish with a few at 5.12 or harder. Cracks, roofs and multi-pitch combinations add variety, and it draws fewer people than the park's most popular faces.

wi_headstone_area.blurb: A bouldering zone on Rib Mountain, near Wausau, south of the overlook tower. The rock is white quartzite, and the area packs 21 problems into a small space: good cracks, powerful faces and fun aretes. It is named for a big leaning block sitting on a pedestal. Difficulty runs from V0 to a couple of very hard outliers, but most problems fall between V1 and V5, so it works for beginners through solid intermediates. Bring a crash pad and wander between the boulders; some problems are tall enough that a rope is a comfort.

_expect.name: Upper Major Mass & Jungle Gym Tower

wi_upper_major_mass_jungle_gym_tower.blurb: The sunny upper level of the Major Mass, with Jungle Gym Tower beside it, below Devil's Doorway on the East Bluff at Devil's Lake. It has 21 routes, nearly all traditional and one top-rope line, with several top-rope setups possible from the shelf the Doorway sits on. Grades run from 5.2 to 5.12, but the majority are 5.4 to 5.8, making it friendly to newer trad leaders. The tower also finishes multi-pitch combinations of up to four pitches rising from the Red Slab. Route-finding through the rocky ridge on the way in is the trickiest part.
